analysis: This PR changes documentation only: docs/provider/cli-reference.md (a one-line doctor/status note at head line ~1274; the supplied head excerpts cover lines 1691-2366+ unchanged context) and docs/reference/provider-authorization.md (new paragraphs after line 91). No executable code, keys, or protocol behavior changes are visible. Security-relevant content: the docs say `darkbloom status`/`doctor` keep displaying an App Attest serving lease until its `expires_at` even when the last renewal is older than `snapshotMaxAge`. `none` and `legacy` decisions still require fresh receipt. MDM-removal advice requires a fresh matching decision plus `mdm_removal_ready`, and `unenroll` rechecks readiness before and after profile inspection. This keeps display of a bounded, unexpired lease separate from the strict removal-readiness gate (related T-053, T-057, A-016). The docs state this is a display/summary behavior, not a change to coordinator authorization, which stays coordinator-owned. They do not weaken the removal gate, since positive removal advice still needs the fresh decision. The residual risk is that a late-but-unexpired lease display could mislead an operator about live serving authorization, but the documentation explicitly separates display from removal readiness. I could not verify the implementation (ProviderAuthorizationReadiness.displayedStatus/summary) because it is not in the supplied evidence. A later pass that sees the code should confirm it matches the docs: expiry is enforced against the observation time, and removal advice never uses the lenient displayed lease. The remaining cli-reference content (the cache env passthrough, the SSD cache documentation consistent with T-041, the sandbox and add-on paths in TB-012/TB-013) appears to be unchanged context. I found no regression or invalidated threat-model assumption.
